newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Stronger Australian bonds run into resistance.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Stronger Australian bonds run into resistance.

text.p: Australian bonds robust recovery from last Friday's U.S payrolls-inspired sell off ran into some technical resistance, but traders said the tone was positive and the market was expected to remain well supported.
Bonds were boosted in offshore trade by a rally in Treasuries, following better than expected U.S. CPI data, and continued to push ahead from the open of floor trading.
However, with bonds recouping their payrolls losses and moving into positive territory, they soon ran into resistance.
"There's a few technical levels up in the mid to low (92.)50s," one trader said of the 10-years rebuffal at 92.525.
Traders said it may only be a pause as the market waited on some key economic data over the remainder of the week.
"There's still a lot stats to come out in the States and we've got labour here tomorrow, so you're not going to get too carried away," the trader said.

December labour force data is due on Thursday. Expectations centre on a 5,000 rise in job numbers and a slight uptick in the unemployment rate to 8.6 percent, a result that would be seen as soft, traders said.
Housing finance data released today showed a 2.9 percent fall in November, but failed to have much of a market impact.

Bond spreads narrower at the long end, as long bonds outperform on the day, despite giving up some early gains. At one stage the curves flattened by over five points in morning trade before the long end ran into resistance and short bonds caught up some ground.
